aspects.says: Each host-initiated network management request is answered by its function, from a list of fields, through its source: a sign-off removes the enabled and logon marks, an unknown function is refused, advices are acknowledged with 0830, and other messages are left to the next listener.
basis: section:15.1 The Host Starts Network Messages Too, and Each One Needs Its Own Answer

aspects.says: A refused sign-on is retried after a wait that doubles with each refusal in a row up to a cap and starts over after a success; the cap is also how long a link may stay out after its host recovers.
basis: section:15.2 A Refused Sign-On Waits Longer Each Time

aspects.says: Doubling by shifting overflows after a few hours of refusals and the delay turns negative, zero or short; doubling step by step inside the cap cannot.
basis: section:15.2.1 Spot the Problem: Doubling by Shifting

aspects.says: A planned stop disables the link, waits with a bound until no request is pending, then signs off and forgets the session; without the drain, approvals in flight are lost and reversed.
basis: section:15.4 Drain a Link Before You Sign It Off

aspects.says: Only echo failures in a row count, an answered echo or a new sign-on starts the count again, and the link is taken out at the limit.
basis: section:15.3 One Lost Echo Is Not a Dead Host

aspects.says: Each failure the echo limit allows keeps a dead host in the pool for one more echo timeout, and every purchase sent there is an unknown outcome to reverse.
basis: section:15.3 One Lost Echo Is Not a Dead Host

aspects.says: A host sign-off that no listener takes ends on the unhandled queue; the link stays enabled and every purchase on it is declined until the logon mark expires.
basis: section:15.1 The Host Starts Network Messages Too, and Each One Needs Its Own Answer

aspects.says: A key change is answered 00 only after the key is imported, its check value matches and it is stored; otherwise it is refused, the old key stays, and the key never travels back in the answer.
basis: section:15.5 A New Key Is Acknowledged Only Once It Is Installed

aspects.says: The lifecycle of a link is down, connected, signed on and stopping, and the ready entry, the logon mark and the enabled mark say which.
basis: section:15.6 The Lifecycle Is a Handful of States, and the Marks Say Which
